title: Burn Your Flags: Interactive CLIs for Agents — Mark Lummus & Navinkumar Patil, PayPal
talk_summary: A PayPal workshop arguing that interactive CLIs break agent harnesses silently (redraw loops instead of questions), and that the fix is to treat agents as a second accessibility persona: expose a machine-readable side channel (JSON state/input), inject context up front, and drive the CLI via tmux send-keys/capture-pane. The strongest transferable point is that tools handed to agents should be deterministic 'small sharp instruments' while the LLM supplies the non-determinism.

takeaways.technique: Side-channel JSON interface for interactive tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of screen-scraping an interactive prompt, the CLI exposes a machine-readable channel (read state, send input as data) so agents get structured JSON rather than a redraw loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: think of side channel as exactly the same ... read state send input as a data

takeaways.technique: tmux send-keys / capture-pane as a universal agent driver
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the interactive CLI detached in a tmux session and have the agent drive it with send-keys and read output with capture-pane, giving persistent sessions and resumability for long-running tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: send keys and capture pain gets you far ... T-Max actually takes a log of those things where it knows what are you working on and resumes those sessions

takeaways.what_they_do: Provide the agent all decision-relevant state (e.g. low inventory, defaults, allowed values) in one machine-readable input file up front, rather than making it discover options through interactive Q&A.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you could provide all this information in one single input file ... this is where we call this as context injection

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the tool itself deterministic and narrowly scoped so the same command always returns the same output; the LLM is the only source of non-determinism.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the CLI is a tool to be used by an LLM, then you absolutely want it to be deterministic ... a small sharp instrument

takeaways.technique: Design tools for mid-tier models, not just frontier
takeaways.what_they_do: They framed the challenge as making the CLI work with a mid-tier model (Haiku/Sonnet class) rather than burning high-thinking tokens on tool driving.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't necessarily want to waste your highinking tokens on running a CLI tool ... can you make Haik coup or sonnet ... run your CLI

takeaways.what_they_do: They ran a live scored leaderboard where correctness plus wall-clock time ranked solutions, which surfaced that a deterministic parser beat LLM-in-the-loop approaches.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an accurate response returned quickly would be biased over an accurate response returned slowly
takeaways.numbers: Winning entries hit ~29-50ms; several scored 3/3 in 0 seconds (gamed)
